title: Symanzik Effective Theory for FCC — Adversarial Round 2

tests.name: R2-A: Plaquette count — 32 distinct triangles from one site
tests.details: Distinct unoriented triangles from one site: 32 (expected 32). Ordered pairs (i<j) with closure: 96. All equilateral: True. Uniform area: True (area = 0.433013 for all). Partners per vector with dot=-1/2: 8. NOTE: 'Per unit cell' count depends on convention: 32/3 ≈ 10.7 (3 sites per triangle), NOT 8 as claimed in Appendix A.3.

tests.name: R2-B: c_1 universality — T_{μν}/z = (1/d)δ_{μν} for both lattices
tests.details: D4 second-moment isotropic: True (max err: 8.88e-16). Cubic second-moment isotropic: True (max err: 0.00e+00). Normalized tensors match: True. T_{μμ}/z: D4 = 0.250000, cubic = 0.250000, expected 1/d = 0.250000. Conclusion: c_1^(0) = 1/12 universality confirmed — both lattices have T_{μν}/z = (1/d)δ_{μν}.

tests.name: R2-C: W(B_4) symmetry (order 384) of FCC propagator
tests.details: |W(B_4)| = 384 (expected 384). Propagator W(B_4)-invariant: True (max violation: 5.33e-15). Single-component sign flips preserve D4: True. Odd sign changes preserving D4 vectors: 8/8 (NOT all — but propagator is still invariant because cos is even).

numerical_data.note: W(B_4) is strictly larger than W(D_4). The propagator has W(B_4) symmetry because single-component sign flips map D4 vectors to D4 vectors, so cos(k·n_i) terms are preserved.
